$comment: Every environment variable a gateway reads, beside its configuration document (GatewayConfig) and the broker variables that document names in signal.userEnv and signal.passwordEnv. A gateway, in any language, reads these and no variable the table does not list — beyond the standard OTEL_* variables an OpenTelemetry SDK reads on its own, and the options variable of the allocator a gateway links (jemalloc's _RJEM_MALLOC_CONF, which it reads before any code of the gateway runs), which the table neither promises nor refuses. `readBy` says what reads each: `gateway`, its own code — which lint:gateway-environment scans in both directions (apps/gateway/src): a read not listed here fails it, and so does a row nothing reads; `opentelemetry`, the OpenTelemetry SDK. `providedBy` says what sets each where the launcher runs a gateway: `launcher` (lint:gateway-environment checks the launcher's boot golden passes it), `image` (the image or its supervisor sets it; checked there too), or `operator` (nothing sets it; an operator may). The conformance suite sets only these, and exercises each by name; one case also sets a variable a gateway's runtime would read for itself (TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS), to show that it changes nothing.

variables.name: JWT_SECRET
variables.effect: The gateway's signing key ring: comma-separated keys of at least 32 characters, whitespace around each ignored. Agent and media tokens are signed with the first key, and a token signed with any key is accepted. Unset, or with a key shorter than 32 characters, the gateway refuses to start.

variables.name: SEMIONT_OIDC_CLIENT_ID
variables.effect: The client id of the gateway's own service account at the issuer, exchanged for the token it reaches the Archivist with. Unset, the gateway refuses to start.

variables.name: SEMIONT_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET
variables.effect: That service account's secret. Unset, the gateway refuses to start, and its output never carries the value.

variables.name: SEMIONT_GATEWAY_CONFIG
variables.effect: The path of the gateway's configuration document, a JSON GatewayConfig. The image sets it to /etc/semiont/gateway.json, where the launcher mounts the document. Unset, the gateway refuses to start and names the variable; there is no default path.

variables.name: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT
variables.effect: The OTLP/HTTP collector spans and metrics are exported to. Unset, with OTEL_CONSOLE_EXPORTER not `true`, nothing is exported.

variables.name: OTEL_SERVICE_NAME
variables.effect: The `service.name` exported spans and metrics carry; `semiont-gateway` when unset.

variables.name: OTEL_SDK_DISABLED
variables.effect: `true` exports nothing, whatever else is set.

variables.name: OTEL_CONSOLE_EXPORTER
variables.effect: `true`, with no OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, writes spans and metrics to the gateway's output instead of exporting them.

variables.name: OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER
variables.effect: `console` writes metrics to the gateway's output, while spans still go to OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT.

variables.name: OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL
variables.effect: Milliseconds between metric exports; 30000 when unset or not a positive integer.

variables.name: OTEL_BSP_SCHEDULE_DELAY
variables.effect: Milliseconds a finished span waits to be exported in a batch; 5000 when unset.

variables.name: SEMIONT_BUS_LOG
variables.effect: Any non-empty value writes one `[bus <op>] <channel> …` line to the gateway's output for each frame it accepts or delivers, and each content read.

variables.name: SUPERVISE_EVENTS
variables.effect: The supervisor's events log, one `starting <SUPERVISE_NAME>` line per life of the process. With SUPERVISE_NAME, the gateway reports `semiont.process.restarts` from it: its lives, less one. Without either, the metric does not exist.

variables.name: SUPERVISE_NAME
variables.effect: The name the supervisor records each life under, in SUPERVISE_EVENTS.
